article_seed.title: Four soldiers wounded in Chaman border bombing as clearance operation continues
article_seed.deck: The border crossing stays shut until Wednesday, with freight backed up on the Pakistani side
article_seed.standfirst: A roadside bomb struck a military vehicle on Monday evening. The military later corrected the police casualty count from three to four.
body: A roadside bomb struck a military vehicle in the Chaman border area on Monday evening, wounding four soldiers, the military's media wing said, correcting an earlier police count of three.

Security forces launched a clearance operation after the blast, the provincial counterterrorism department said. The military said on Tuesday that the operation was continuing and gave no timeline for reopening the border crossing.
The district administration said the crossing would remain closed until Wednesday morning. Traders said hundreds of trucks were waiting on the Pakistani side.

Two of the wounded soldiers were in stable condition at a Quetta hospital, according to the military account. A hospital official, speaking on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to brief media, said two wounded soldiers were treated and discharged on Monday night. That account could not be independently corroborated.
No group had claimed responsibility.
The channel initially reported that the operation had ended, then published a correction saying it was continuing.

messages.text: Update: The military's media wing says four soldiers were wounded, correcting an earlier police count of three. Two are in stable condition at a Quetta hospital. No group has claimed responsibility.
Photographs released by the department show the damaged vehicle and security personnel at the scene. The images have not been independently verified.

The federal cabinet approved a national digital records policy on Tuesday, requiring ministries to publish procurement notices in a searchable format within 90 days. Information Minister Ayesha Raza said the policy would improve transparency and shorten records requests.

The cabinet also approved funding for a new weather radar network in Gilgit-Baltistan. The finance ministry put the programme cost at 4.2 billion rupees over three years.

The State Bank held its policy rate at 19.5 percent on Monday, citing persistent inflation. Inflation was 12.8 percent in September, according to the bureau of statistics. The bank said food prices remained the main pressure and left the door open to a review in December.

article_seed.title: A hold, not yet a pivot for monetary policy
article_seed.deck: The central bank is waiting for supply conditions, not demand, to ease
body: The central bank's decision leaves borrowing costs unchanged for a fourth consecutive meeting.
The statement points to food prices rather than demand as the main pressure, which suggests the committee is waiting for supply conditions to ease before moving.
That interpretation is supported by the September inflation figure cited in the bank's own statement, but the bank has not published its internal forecast.

article_seed.title: Border closures need a published contingency plan
article_seed.deck: An editorial on the cost of unexplained shutdowns
body: The border closure is a reminder that trade routes need contingency plans.
The government should publish a clear reopening timeline and compensate small traders who cannot absorb another week of losses.
A closure that lasts without explanation damages confidence as much as the closure itself.
